instructions: The night before, or at least 1 hour ahead: whisk the 1 2/3 cups flour, 3 tbsp of the sugar and the 1/4 tsp salt together in a large bowl.
Make a well in the middle and crack in the 3 eggs. Whisk the eggs, pulling in a little flour from the sides as you go, until you have a thick paste.

Pour in the 2 cups milk a little at a time, whisking after each pour, until the batter is smooth with no lumps. Whisk in 1/3 cup water and the 2 tbsp oil. It should be thin, glossy and pourable, and lightly coat the back of a spoon.
Cover the bowl and leave it on the counter for 1 hour, or put it in the fridge overnight. If it's been in the fridge, take it out about an hour before you cook.
Cut the lemon into wedges and put them on the table with 1/4 cup of the sugar in a small bowl.
Whisk the batter again. It thickens as it sits, so if it no longer runs easily off the spoon, whisk in a splash of water.
Heat a 9 or 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium high. Melt about 1/2 tsp of the butter in it, then wipe most of it away with a paper towel so only a thin shine is left.
Lift the pan off the heat and pour about 1/4 cup of batter into the middle. Straight away, tilt and swirl the pan so the batter runs out into a thin, even circle, and set it back on the heat.
Cook for 45 seconds to 1 minute, until the edges look dry and the underside is pale golden with brown speckles.
Slide a long thin spatula under the crepe and flip it. Cook the other side for about 30 seconds, then slide it onto a plate.

Keep going with the rest of the batter, adding a little butter to the pan each time and stacking the crepes as they come out. You'll get about 15. The first one is a test, so if it browns too fast, turn the heat down a little.
Fold the crepes into quarters or roll them up, and serve warm with the lemon wedges and sugar. Stack any leftovers with parchment between them and keep them in the fridge for up to 3 days.
advance_prep_notes: Make the batter the night before, or at least 1 hour ahead, so it can rest.
method_notes: All three make a thin batter of flour, eggs, milk, a little sugar and salt plus fat, and cook about 1/4 cup at a time in a lightly buttered nonstick pan, swirled thin, about a minute on the first side and under 30 seconds on the second. RecipeTin Eats (JB's crêpes) whisks it by hand with water and oil and rests it 1 hour or overnight; Once Upon a Chef blends it with melted butter and vanilla and rests it 30 minutes to 24 hours; Natasha's Kitchen blends it and skips the rest. Lemon and sugar is the plain French way to serve them. For savory fillings like ham and cheese, cut the sugar in the batter to 1 tbsp.
